{"notes": "VISIT 1 (1:45). Fish: belly line and lower tail fork are connected to the start (dark). Top body line is pale, not connected: gap at the nose, and it stops near x=14.7, short of the tail. The upper tail fork and its joint are also pale, not connected. 10 min limit, so the top line and upper fork still need finishing.

MAYA: Says she drew the sketch, assigned strokes, and is on the top line. Her status report ('on track') was too rosy: her own line is disconnected at the nose and unfinished. She didn't flag the gap; Priya did. Her plan to inspect the tail joint is sensible, but the joint isn't ready. Good for planning and delegation. Execution and checking of her own work is a concern. Check on the next visit whether she has finished the top line.

TOM: Has the belly line, which is solidly connected and appears done, plus the lower fork. He understated progress ('a few more to reach the tail joint') in a harmless way. Good plan to walk the whole run from the nose to verify connectivity. His hands were at the upper fork tip, which is not connected at its joint. Don't know who placed what. Check whether he follows through on the walk-through.

PRIYA: Proactively spotted the unlinked dominoes at the nose, announced it publicly, and said she was closing the gap. That is strong collaboration and ownership beyond her assigned tail fork. Verify next visit that the gap is actually closed.

LEO: Said nothing and I saw nothing from him. No evidence either way. Assigned a tail fork; the upper fork is disconnected. Ask him directly next visit and watch for his contribution. Don't rate him down for lack of observation."}
